title: Effective theories: proof search and decision procedures

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel’s Theorems
based_on.pages: 33–35 (§§4.3–4.5, Theorems 4.1–4.2); 304–306 (§40.5, Theorems 40.6–40.7); corrected second-edition reprint, August 2020

summary: Enumerate formal consequences, turn completeness into a terminating proof search, and decide equality and dense-order sentences by explicit quantifier elimination.
abstract: Checking a finished proof and finding a proof are different tasks. If a theory’s axioms can be listed by a program, we can systematically search all its finite proofs, eventually finding every consequence. A search that has found nothing, however, does not tell us whether a proof exists. For a consistent theory that settles every sentence, searching for a proof of the sentence and its negation together gives a decision procedure. We prove that this search terminates and then develop more direct procedures for infinite sets with equality alone and for dense linear orders without endpoints. Their quantifiers can be removed by finite manipulations of formulas, leaving a Boolean calculation for each sentence.
